Use case: illustration-story. Three production scene paintings arranged as exactly THREE equal-width edge-to-edge TALL portraits side by side, each 390:844 aspect. No gutters, lines, borders, labels or text. Input image1 is Mars laboratory ROOM/style reference. Image2 equipment reference for cream metal, cobalt science fittings and realistic modest wear. Each portrait contains fixed room architecture and equipment only in UPPER 40%, lower 60% broad quiet clean grey floor for game objects. Features must be legible at phone size and within central 82% width of each portrait. Realistic restrained retro-industrial rendering, coherent light, no people, floating tools or specimens outside containment. Not decorative futuristic holograms.
LEFT: initial discovery laboratory inside the repaired cream starter habitat. At x27%, y29%, a wall-fixed RAW WATER STRAINER service housing has a clear small inspection chamber packed with brown flecks and silt, two connected pipes through wall, capped backflush port; visibly upstream of a separate treatment cabinet partly at far left. At x72%, y28%, a substantial cobalt-and-cream optical laboratory MICROSCOPE stands fixed on a clean bench recessed into wall. Microscope has eyepieces, objective and empty specimen stage under a transparent enclosure; make physical microscope unmistakable, not just a computer. Sealed small circular window reveals red terrain. No giant brown creature or sample already under optics. Broad empty floor below.
MIDDLE: reference core return between nearby ice and lab freezer. Camera inside same clean habitat service threshold. Upper LEFT contains a wide clear closed pressure window looking directly toward an accessible LOW pale blue-white ice bank beside—but visibly away from—the resource well. The unheated bank margin is visible around x28%,y25%; the bore casing lies farther away at far left, no melt cavity visible. Upper RIGHT at x72%,y28% contains an open-fronted refrigerated cabinet behind a clear cold transfer screen, one empty horizontal WHOLE CORE cradle inside, cobalt seals, a separate small closed membrane-holder drawer beneath. All precision lab equipment is visibly INDOORS; outdoor ice separated by window/airlock wall. No naked sample in air, no core already in cradle. Lower floor quiet.
RIGHT: same laboratory returned from expedition, now viewed toward two cold science stations. LEFT x27%,y28% a contained chilled preparation glovebox with transparent sealed front, simple service transfer port and EMPTY flat cradle; RIGHT x72%,y28% a large cold optical microscope with visible eyepieces/objective, illuminated transmitted-light stage within a clear contained enclosure. Freezer cabinet at rear edge remains closed, with small membrane-holder drawer separate. Crisp cobalt seals distinguish cold science hardware, cream structure remains family. No specimen, body, ice cylinder, field case or changed anatomy already painted; these are movable objects. Clear lower floor.
All equipment here was imported precision equipment; no locally fabricated microscope or freezer. Maintain one recognizable laboratory family and actual distinct working surfaces. No food utensils, farming roots, mixed specimen vessels or warehouse-scale machinery.
